title: Bound state of a He-3 atom at free He-4 surfaces
abstract: Quantum Monte Carlo simulations confirm the existence of a bound state of a single He-3 atom at a free superfluid He-4 surface in three dimensions, localized within a ~10-A thick low-density He-4 surface layer, with a binding energy of approximately 4 K with respect to vacuum. As the temperature is raised above ~ 1 K the He-3 atom leaves the surface to dissolve into the superfluid. The situation is entirely different in two dimensions, as the He-3 atom is excluded from the superfluid and no surface bound state exists. Results are also presented for the a He-3 atom binding to nanoscale size He-4 clusters adsorbed on weak substrates, a physical system that may allow for the observation of some of the physics predicted for extended surfaces. It is shown that a He-3 bound state localized at the perimeter of sufficiently small (a few tens of atoms) clusters exists not just on Cs, as previously reported, but on all alkali substrates.
summary: This paper uses Quantum Monte Carlo simulations to determine if a He-3 atom forms a bound state at the surface of superfluid He-4. It finds a robust bound state in 3D but demonstrates that this state disappears entirely when the system is reduced to two dimensions. The study also extends these findings to small clusters, showing strong dependence on the substrate material.
main_problem: The study investigates the existence and properties of a bound state for a single He-3 atom interacting with the surface of superfluid He-4, comparing 3D, 2D, and nanoscale cluster geometries.
main_result: A bound state exists at the 3D free surface with a binding energy of ~4 K, but this state vanishes in 2D and is highly dependent on the substrate interaction in nanoscale clusters.
method: The research primarily employs Quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations, specifically using the continuous-space Worm Algorithm, to calculate thermodynamic properties and binding energies.
model_or_system: The system models He-3 atoms interacting with He-4 superfluid surfaces, ranging from infinite 3D free surfaces to finite nanoscale clusters adsorbed on alkali substrates (Cs, Li).
key_observables: Binding energy ($\Delta$ or $\epsilon$), He-4 density profiles ($ho(z)$), and the He-3 probability density of position ($|\Psi_3(z)|^2$).
important_parameters: Temperature ($T$), dimensionality (3D vs 2D), and the strength of the substrate interaction.
main_assumptions: The simulations use established interatomic potentials (e.g., Aziz pair potential) and rely on QMC techniques to handle the quantum nature of the superfluid.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate density profiles and the spatial localization of the He-3 atom at various temperatures and for different cluster sizes/substrates, showing confinement near the surface edge.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares results across different dimensionalities: first establishing the 3D free surface case, then contrasting it with the 2D case, and finally extending the analysis to finite nanoscale clusters on various substrates.
why_interesting: This work provides detailed insights into how dimensionality and confinement affect quantum surface phenomena, which is crucial for understanding quantum adsorption and surface-mediated interactions in quantum fluids.
